(B) "Laal is characterised by strong stem-initial prominence (Lionnet & Hyman 2018: 651–655 and references therein), mostly of a distributional nature: the number of consonantal and vocalic contrasts is much greater stem-initially than elsewhere, as shown in (4) above. The stem is defined as a lexical root and any suffixes attached to it (there are no prefixes). Most morphological words involve only one stem, e.g. /nō/ ‘person’, /gùm-ál/ ‘melon-SG.’ ... Stems in Laal are maximally disyllabic. ... Finally, Laal has three contrastive tone heights: high (H), mid (M), and low (L), illustrated in the minimal triplet in (8) below. ... The tone-bearing unit is the mora"

new_statements.rule_in_words: Laal is a three-tone language (H/M/L, mora as TBU) which its principal modern describer classifies as having no stress; the only prominence described is stem-initial (= word-initial, there being no prefixes) and is distributional: the full consonant inventory, the full 12-vowel inventory and the vowel-length contrast occur only in the stem-initial C1V1, with reduced inventories and no length elsewhere; stems are maximally disyllabic.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. About 50 loanword stems exceed the disyllabic maximum; Boyeldieu 1982 (excerpt pp.5-7) likewise gives three distinctive tone heights and initial-position maximal inventories without mentioning accent.
new_statements.domain_note: Prominence is stated over the stem (root + suffixes; no prefixes, so stem-initial coincides with word-initial); statement (A) is a passing typological classification in a cross-linguistic database chapter, by the same author who did 18 months of fieldwork on Laal; (B) is the dedicated Laal description. Neither reports acoustic correlates of stress.
new_statements.identity_note: All Lionnet sources describe Laal as spoken mainly in Gori (with Damtar), matching Boyeldieu's 'laal de Gori'; Boyeldieu 1982's consultant was a native of Damtar. Same language, laal1242; the near-extinct Laabe variety of Damtar is not separately described. Note: Lionnet 2020 'Kulaale Language Snapshot' (LDD 17) is about Fania (fani1244), not Laal, despite appearing in his Laal-era bibliography.

sources.note: Sec. 2.2 (p.4-5 of draft): 'The stem-initial C1V1 sequence can thus be defined as a position of prominence in Laal'; 'Laal is a tonal language, with a three-way high vs. mid vs. low contrast. The Tone Bearing Unit is the mora.' Conclusion: tripartite strength within stem (pre-V2 strongest, V2 weakest). No use of the term stress for Laal.
